text:
Aisha Patel: Heads up — spotted systematic disagreement from the quantized judge (j-3b-q8) on the synthetic contradiction anchors. :thinking:
Tom Nguyen: can you paste a couple of examples? is this new after the q8 move or always flaky?
Aisha Patel: New after q8 rollout last night. Before quant we were at 92% agreement with human anchors, now ~74%. Quick sample: 'I ate an apple' vs 'I did not eat an apple' gets labeled as EQUIV by the judge sometimes.
Devon Lee: ugh, that sounds like the KV cache mismatch we saw before when the runner reused context buffers across threads. Could be a runner bug re: seed/temperature propagation in concurrent jobs.
Priya Rao: CI runs show flake on the judge suite too — the eval-runner logs show identical seed in the header for multiple tasks: 
```
# eval-runner config excerpt
parallel_workers: 8
rng_seed: 42  # accidentally fixed for all workers in v0.3.7
cache_prefixing: enabled
```
Priya Rao: if rng_seed is reused across workers you can get correlated outputs which amplifies quant noise.
EvalBot: automated-run: 2145679002 — j-3b: unquantized acc 0.92, j-3b-q8 acc 0.75, delta -0.17; p<0.01 vs baseline; sample_size=1200.
Marco Silva: interesting. could be two things: 1) quantization-induced calibration shift in logits, 2) eval harness amplification because of seed reuse + batching.
Tom Nguyen: agree. worth validating by re-running one-worker at varying seeds and comparing distributions. also let's add an adversarial paraphrase set to check tie-break flakiness.
Aisha Patel: I've started that locally. Preliminary: single-worker runs (no parallel) keep agreement ~90% even with q8, so runner parallelism is a prime suspect.
Devon Lee: bug story: earlier patch in runner v0.3.7 disabled per-worker RNG when using continuous batching. I'll open a PR to remove the global seed and thread-localize rng.
Priya Rao: also proposing a short-term mitigation in judge selection: if primary judge is quantized and shows >10% drop vs baseline on anchor suite, fallback to ensemble (primary+calibrated smaller model) for adjudication.
Marco Silva: ensemble fallback is fine but expensive. Could we instead apply a lightweight calibration layer on logits coming from q models? temperature scaling on judge outputs might recover parity.
Tom Nguyen: yes — try temperature scaling + reranking using embedding similarity anchors. we should also add an eval-harness metric that tracks "anchor flip rate" (fraction of anchor pairs that change label after quant/runner change).
Aisha Patel: actionable: (1) Devon to PR runner rng fix (2) Priya to add anchor-flip metric + CI gate (3) Marco to prototype temp-scaling on q judges (4) Tom to run reproducibility sweep with single-worker seeds.
Devon Lee: PR opened: https://git.redwood/.com/eng/eval-runner/pulls/482 — includes tests that simulate parallel worker seeds.
Priya Rao: I'll add the metric and a threshold check in the CI job: fail if anchor_flip_rate > 0.08 for judge bringup.
EvalBot: CI note — job eval/judge-smoke updated to run anchors before merge.
Aisha Patel: thanks team. let's reconvene tomorrow after PR + single-worker runs. :thumbsup:
